recipes.title: One sentence to a short film
recipes.pitch: Write one sentence. Get a 20 to 30 second film: a written shot list, one character, moving shots, a score, cut on the beat.
recipes.why: Every step is a model you can open: the language model writes the shots, Klein draws one character and keeps it through every keyframe, H3 moves each frame, Music 3 scores it, and the cuts land on beats measured in the song.

fields.label: Your sentence
fields.default: An old lamplighter rows through a flooded city at night, relighting its lanterns one by one until the whole skyline glows gold.

tips: The shot list is yours to change before you press Run.
Give the character clothing and colours you would know from behind: that is what stays the same from shot to shot.
Each shot's own sound is kept quietly under the score.

recipes.title: Perfect loop
recipes.pitch: One still becomes a clip that ends where it began, with the seam measured.
recipes.why: The first frame and the last frame are the same picture, so the model has to come home. A short fade closes the small gap the model leaves, and SSIM across the seam is reported before and after.

fields.label: What loops
fields.default: a small floating island with a waterfall pouring off its edge into a sea of clouds, one gnarled tree on top, golden light, dark teal sky

models.licence: MiniMax H3 Community License
models.note: Show the name in commercial products. Read the licence's territory terms before you rely on it.

models.name: ffmpeg
models.licence: LGPL/GPL, runs as a separate tool

tips: No person and no camera move: both break a loop first (the owner's own rule from his loop maker).
Chaotic motion like rain shows a reset unless faded.

steps.label: First frame = last frame
steps.model: MiniMax H3 first and last frame

steps.label: Close the seam
steps.what: Fades the tail of the clip into its head and measures the seam.

tested.note: First and last frame of the loop: SSIM 0.962, PSNR 45.1 dB, against 48.2 dB between neighbouring frames. Before the seam step the same frames read SSIM 0.855, PSNR 31.0 dB. Sound measured at -16 LUFS, not judged by ear.

expected.basis: sum of each step's measured time on this box, with a cold start per step

recipes.title: Storyboard to one continuous shot
recipes.pitch: Three boards of one place, then one unbroken shot that travels through them.
recipes.why: Each later board is redrawn from the one before, so the cottage and the tree stay where they were. The second clip starts on the real last frame of the first, and a short dissolve hides what is left of the join; the number is measured.

recipes.title: VFX stack on a generated plate
recipes.pitch: Generate a street, empty it, turn it to night, flood it. Every stage side by side.
recipes.why: LTX-2.5's IC-LoRAs are made to be stacked: each pass takes the last pass's clip as its source. The grid shows one plate through three effects.

recipes.title: Product ad from nothing
recipes.pitch: A hero still, the same product moving, a second camera on the same moment, a score, cut on the beat.
recipes.why: Reshoot films the first clip again from a new angle, so the product in the second shot is the same one, not a lookalike. That is what keeps an ad from falling apart.

fields.label: The product
fields.default: a faceted perfume bottle of smoked glass with a gold cap and no label

tips: Plain surfaces with no print: blank products invent logos when they are told nothing.
Name the product's shape and colours in the second camera's words too, and keep the move small: a wide orbit invents the far side of the bottle.
Reshoot is the slow step, about 8 minutes here.

steps.label: Cut on the beat
steps.what: Finds the tempo and beats in the song, picks its loudest section, and cuts each clip on a beat. Loudness normalized.

tested.note: A smoked-glass bottle with a gold cap on wet black stone, then the reshoot's second camera on the same moment, cut on the beat. Frames checked at 3 per second: the bottle keeps its shape, cap and colours across both shots, and there is no text or logo anywhere. The second camera's dolly back barely shows, so the two shots read as one slow hero shot. Sound measured at -14.7 LUFS, not judged by ear.

expected.basis: sum of each step's measured time on this box, with a cold start per step

recipes.title: Music Video Maker
recipes.pitch: A song with your words, one character, seven directed shots, cut on the beat: a 30 to 45 second music video.
recipes.why: The song comes first and the picture follows it. Music 3 sings as long as the lyrics last, so the words set the length. Klein keeps one character through every keyframe, H3 moves each frame with its own camera move, and the edit is measured from the song: tempo, beats, its loudest section, then loudness normalized.

[chorus]
Take me to the gold line, take me to the sea
Every mile of midnight is a mile closer to me
Take me to the gold line, hold the morning near
I can see the city, I can see it clear
[verse]
Moon on the desert, silver and wide
Nobody's waiting on the other side
[chorus]
Take me to the gold line, take me to the sea
Every mile of midnight is a mile closer to me
Take me to the gold line, hold the morning near
I can see the city, I can see it clear
[outro]

recipes.title: One take, two cameras
recipes.pitch: Shoot once, film it again with the camera moving, cut between them on one sound track.
recipes.why: Reshoot keeps the action and the timing, so the two takes cut together at the same timecode, like two cameras on one set.

tips: One clear action reads best from a second angle.
Keep camera B's move small, like a push in: a wide orbit has to invent the far side of the set, and it shows.

steps.label: Cut between
steps.what: Cuts between takes of one moment on one sound track.

tested.note: A cook tossing noodles under a red awning, filmed once locked off and again by the reshoot pushing in, cut four times on one sound track. Frames checked at 4 per second and at full size: the same face, apron, awning and bulbs in both cameras, hands whole on the wok, no text. Camera B ends close on the cook with the wok below the frame.
